title: Measuring What Matters: Capture-Aware Evaluation Validity in Machine-Learning Intrusion and Breach Detection, Necessary Conditions Derived from Seven Benchmark Audits
content: Machine-learning intrusion and breach detectors are often reported at near-ceiling accuracy, yet a score supports a deployment decision only if its evaluation measures the intended generalisation. We integrate seven companion audits, covering eleven public collections from nine source captures in four data modalities, and derive the conditions an evaluation must meet for its score to be interpretable. Four domains recurred: protocol (does the split test the stated target?), acquisition (are labels separable from capture conditions?), operational (does performance hold at a stated false-alarm budget and prevalence?) and label (do labels reflect the mechanism or the annotator?). In a structural causal model, acquisition–label aliasing makes deployment performance non-identifiable, and only annihilating aggregators respect this non-compensatory structure. No collection passed all four domains; protocol effects depended on task rather than model; and precursor-stage attacks, the early-warning target for ransomware, were detected at about half the rate of impact-stage attacks at 1% false-alarm rate. We provide a 28-item audit instrument with a seven-item minimum viable audit and falsification criteria. The framework is derived, not yet validated.
